Brahmyodha: The Destroyer.topper: The three topper openings use three complementary architectures: (1) Devraj Indra and Acharya Thama react with shock to an ordinary boy opening a 5,000-year sealed power book; (2) the villain Aaka and Dudusi discuss the missing Agni Shakti book, then connect it to Vidyut and the unknown thief; (3) Nagarjun vows to awaken the dead to stop Vidyut because the apparently poor boy has obtained something dangerous. In all three, an antagonist/authority reacts first, a forbidden artifact or hidden force creates the question, and Vidyut's unknown identity becomes the spine. Escalate through a compact chain of artifact/test -> Vidyut choice or bodily power proof -> mentor/royal reaction -> approaching enemy or next trial. Finish on a concrete object, mark, book, box, enemy or identity reveal, followed by specific questions and Pocket FM CTA.
Brahmyodha: The Destroyer.average: The average cohort contains real Brahmyodha material and often a strong ending, but does not sustain the topper compression and causal spine. 'BY_fir se janam' has an excellent mother-resurrecting-dead-child opening and a clear final arrival of the feared enemy, yet jumps across Vidyut's life and spends less time on a visible hero decision. 'Vidyut ka janam' has cinematic labor, deception and locket-breaking action, but carries heavy production detail, many characters and a long route before the central threat resolves into the cliffhanger. 'CHANA CHOR GARAM' has a distinctive comic Vidyut voice, training and a powerful seven-chakra/locket theft payoff, but its long direction-heavy structure and comedy-to-epic tonal shift dilute momentum. Average scripts should score above rejected when the emotional premise, source-specific artifact and final danger are clear, while deductions remain for middle drag, spoon-feeding, tonal inconsistency or weak bridges.
Brahmyodha: The Destroyer.belowAverage: The four below-average scripts show that isolated spectacle is not enough. Ghamandi Aishwarya has a workable royal challenge but becomes a long, repetition-heavy competition before a serpent attack weakly connected to the opening. Son of Fire has strong stone-breaking and Naagrani-sacrifice images but is an extension dependent on prior context, with long explanation and stacked powers and names. The two Thama Ki Shart versions use generic poor-boy/royal marriage humiliation, multi-stage competition and episode-style development; their strongest moral dilemma or red-fog illusion arrives late, after repeated insults, resolved contest beats and heavy direction. Across the cohort, production-note density, spoon-fed narration, too many characters and locations, weak causal bridges and broad CTA questions after a diluted climax create low pattern fit.

parameterSignals.Hook: Prefer an authority/villain's shocked reaction to a specific forbidden artifact or threat. A royal challenge or poor-boy marriage insult is below-average when it remains a generic status scene and does not quickly introduce Vidyut's artifact, identity or supernatural danger.
parameterSignals.Context & World Clarity: Quickly connect Vidyut's poor/ordinary appearance, missing parents or protected identity, the artifact/competition, and why Thama, Nagarjun or the gods fear his potential.
parameterSignals.Sequence & Plot Movement: Topper chain is challenge or threat -> Vidyut decision -> power/identity clue -> new danger. Below-average sequences accumulate competitions, years of backstory, episode summaries and location changes; a strong late stone break, serpent attack or illusion does not repair a chain where earlier scenes do not cause the next consequence.
parameterSignals.Scene Design: Compact action/reaction/consequence scenes are required. Penalize scenes that contain only a challenge, explanation or SFX list, and penalize a cinematic finale when it is an extension, disconnected from the opening, or preceded by resolved contest beats.
parameterSignals.Pacing & Transitions: Reward a strong final acceleration, but deduct when a life-stage jump, labor-to-childhood transition, long training block, production instruction, or comedy-to-epic shift interrupts the emotional build.
parameterSignals.Ending, Callback & CTA: End on one concrete danger or identity reveal and targeted questions. Below-average endings list every unresolved character, power and location after a diluted or already-resolved climax; an extension that assumes a previous promo is not a strong standalone callback.
parameterSignals.Narration/Dialogue Balance: Narration gives concise bridges; dialogue performs challenge, warning, confession, decision or reveal.
parameterSignals.Mental Impact & Recall Value: Leave the contrast of ordinary/poor Vidyut versus forbidden power, plus one image such as the glowing book, five elemental marks, lightning, or the father's sealed box.
parameterSignals.Follow successful promos pattern: Low pattern fit is signaled by a generic humiliation headline, extension-only context, repeated competition beats, dense production instructions, long spoon-fed narration, tonal or location drift, and a late spectacle that is not causally earned.

7.0 - 7.5: Arjun Ki Shaadi V2_Script + PS_Ankit Pal_Tandrima.docx

King of Dragon.topper: The three topper promos use different entry hooks but converge on a very effective King of Dragon architecture. 'Bhikhari Pati' opens as gossip: one crore per night for a poor man to become a billionaire's contract husband, then uses selected episode beats to reach public insult, gunfire and a masked army. The other two foreground Arjun's betrayal/mother-protection rage and the same high-impact status reversal: Arjun attacks Naren, is shot, a distant shooter fires back, helicopters arrive, and a wealthy Mask Man recognizes the Dragon locket and abducts Arjun and Shivanya. The common chain is gossip or betrayal hook -> clear Arjun/Shivanya relationship pressure -> Arjun makes a protective or rage-driven choice -> visible public consequence -> unexpected rescue/interruption -> Dragon locket/hidden identity recognition -> forced movement into a new danger. The final interruption is more important than resolving the fight; it should leave the listener asking who the Mask Man is and what Arjun's Dragon King connection means.
King of Dragon.average: Clear Arjun/Shivanya premise and some strong curiosity, but setup is over-invested, timeline less clear, or the strongest Dragon King proof arrives late. Ending may work while the middle remains summary-heavy.
King of Dragon.belowAverage: Often spends too long on repeated in-law/fiancée insults, poverty labels, character lists or broad Dragon King mythology. A usable scene is buried in exposition, too many names are introduced, and generic questions follow a resolved or diffused conflict.

parameterSignals.Hook: Concrete gossip or betrayal beats generic poor-husband setup: one crore per night for a contract husband, Arjun's mother being insulted, or a status mystery that makes Shivanya's choice urgent.
parameterSignals.Context & World Clarity: Make Arjun's apparent poverty, Shivanya's wealth/relationship pressure, Misha/Kabir betrayal or family insult, and the Dragon locket's hidden significance understandable before the final reversal.
parameterSignals.Sequence & Plot Movement: Topper chain is gossip/betrayal -> relationship pressure -> Arjun protects or erupts -> bullets/visible consequence -> counter-shooter and helicopters -> Mask Man recognizes locket -> abduction/new threat. Do not resolve the public fight before introducing the larger mystery.
parameterSignals.Scene Design: Use a public insult or contract scene, a motivated Arjun reaction, an unmistakable physical consequence, then an oversized Mask Man/helicopter interruption. The Mask Man must do something—recognize the locket and take the couple—not merely be described.
parameterSignals.Pacing & Transitions: Let betrayal or mother-protection motivate Arjun's rage, then compress the action into bullet -> countershot -> helicopters -> masked arrival. Selected episode inserts can work only when each one advances the same relationship-to-identity spine.
parameterSignals.Ending, Callback & CTA: The strongest topper ending is an unresolved forced abduction and locket recognition, followed by specific questions about the Mask Man's identity and motive, Arjun's Dragon King connection, Shivanya's fate and the next danger, plus Pocket FM CTA.
parameterSignals.Narration/Dialogue Balance: Short dialogue handles insult, curiosity, promise, shock and reveal; narration compresses backstory.
parameterSignals.Mental Impact & Recall Value: The durable memory is insulted/poor Arjun turning violently protective, then the bullet-and-helicopter reversal and Mask Man seeing the Dragon locket. Shivanya remains part of the danger rather than a detached romance subplot.
parameterSignals.Follow successful promos pattern: High fit requires the personal marriage/betrayal engine to cause Arjun's action and the final Dragon locket/Mask Man reversal. Generic rich-family humiliation, repeated power exposition, or a Dragon King name without this status-reversal chain does not qualify.
